scope: Strict-single-hop-only PQ and exact-rerank tie policy after expanded retention and exact-L capacity fixes. Local code/tests only; no native operations or benchmark run by this agent.

implementation.pq: A stateless crate-private NeighborPriorityQueue::insert_with_id_ties orders by distance then ID. It retains the SIMD distance lower bound and refines equal-distance suffixes with a binary search. Only SingleHopFilterSearch calls it, for seeds and discovered matching neighbors.
implementation.exact: RerankAndFilter opts into distance-then-dataset-ID ordering only in strict expanded/frontier constructors. Associated data is not a tie key.
implementation.unchanged_defaults: Existing NeighborPriorityQueue::insert comparisons and all established disk-mode postprocessor sort policies are unchanged. Common buffer insertion was factored into an inline helper without a policy branch on ordinary insert.
implementation.scratch_reuse: There is no stored queue ordering flag. Strict and ordinary insertion methods choose the policy per call on a cleared queue; reuse cannot leak a strict policy into another mode.
implementation.retained_guards: Exact-L queue capacity, pre-PQ membership checks, visited deduplication, and cache-only strict expanded reranking remain in place.

checks: higher tied ID rejected at full boundary
lower tied ID inserts before already expanded tie
ordinary insert after clear retains its legacy tie policy

before_after_regressions.oracle: independent full sort by (distance, ID), truncated to capacity

validation.dependency_notice: proc-macro-error2 reports a future-incompatibility notice; the successful clippy check has no denied warnings.

previous_expanded_exact_l_review.scope: Preserved as intermediate implementation evidence; its source hashes are not the current tie-order source hashes.

native_dump_tie_analysis.scope: Independent C++ agent analysis of the earlier expanded candidate build before exact-L/tie-policy fixes; does not benchmark this new implementation.

performance_claim: Pending root-coordinated native measurements. Matching tie semantics can affect both traversal and strict-ID recall; the local tests do not establish numerical throughput or recall changes on the 10M dataset.
